# The components tier starts three runners only to report a skip

## Context

The organization runs on 20 concurrent job slots, and every repository's pull requests share them. A runner booted only to report a skip is a slot another pull request waits for. Epic #20328 holds an Engine PR push to the slots its diff needs. #20338 gave `unit`, `e2e-engine` and `e2e-brain` job-level skips. Its intake (#20338 comment 6665796895) left `components` for later, because skipping a sharded tier also changes its required contexts.

That is not a choice between shapes. A skipped matrix never reports its per-shard contexts, so under the cap the tier needs one aggregate context. #17171 binds the guards the same way.

## The Problem

`test.yml`'s `test` job is a three-shard matrix with no job-level `if:`. Each shard gates its steps on `matrix.run`, so a PR the classifier rules out of the tier still boots three runners. Each runner only verifies the head and prints a skip. Measured on #20574 (docs only, head `35fd47a0ec`): `components (1/3)`, `(2/3)` and `(3/3)` each held a runner for about 5 s, and every test step was skipped.

A job-level `if:` alone would strand those PRs. The `dev` ruleset requires each shard by name: `components (1/3)`, `(2/3)` and `(3/3)` (`GET /repos/neomjs/neo/rules/branches/dev`, 2026-11-08T18:06Z). A matrix skipped before expansion reports one check under its unexpanded name. On the same head, that check is `e2e-engine (${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ matrix.shards }})`. So no `components (n/3)` context would ever report.

## The Architectural Reality

- `.github/workflows/test.yml` `test`: matrix `include` of three components entries. Its `name:` and artifact name still carry the `tzLabel` and `suite` generality the timezone probes needed before #20355 moved them into `unit`.
- `.github/workflows/test-e2e.yml` `e2e-engine` + `e2e-engine-gate`: the shape to copy. The shards skip at job level. The gate (`if: always()`, `needs: [changes, e2e-engine]`) reports the one required context. It accepts `skipped` only on an explicit `run_e2e=false` from a successful classifier.
- `.github/workflows/classify-test-scope.yml` emits `run_components` and `skip_reason`. A stale head sets every run flag to `false` with its reason.
- `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/util/WorkflowScopeClassifier.spec.mjs` holds the e2e tier to that shape: job `if:`, head-gated steps, and the gate script executed across every verdict.

## The Fix

1. The matrix job, renamed `components`, skips at job level unless `run_components` is `'true'` and a dispatch probe selects no other suite. Its steps drop the `matrix.run` and dead `suite`/`tz` arms and keep the head gate.
2. A `components-gate` job named `components`, in the `e2e-engine-gate` shape, reports the tier's one context.
3. `WorkflowScopeClassifier.spec.mjs` gains the two e2e arms for the components tier, red on `dev` first.
4. Ruleset (operator, at merge): `components (1/3)`, `(2/3)` and `(3/3)` out, `components` in. #17171's baseline swap needs an edit at the same moment, so one edit can carry both.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: The matrix job skips at job level on a ruled-out verdict, and every step that spends the runner stays gated on the live head. A spec holds both, red on `dev`.
- [x] AC-2: The `components` gate passes skipped shards only on `run_components=false` from a successful classifier. It passes run shards only when all succeeded. Every other combination fails. A spec executes the gate script across those verdicts, red on `dev`.
- [x] AC-3: The PR body records the check names GitHub reports on the PR's own head.
- [x] AC-4 (post-merge): The first ruled-out PR after the merge starts no components runner, and its `components` context is green with the classifier's reason.
- [x] AC-5 (post-merge, operator): The ruleset swap is shown by `gh api repos/neomjs/neo/rules/branches/dev` output.

## Out of Scope

- The classifier's `run_components` predicate (#20329, #20330).
- The baseline's contexts and the guard workflows (#17171).
- Shard count and balance (#18916).

## Avoided Traps

- **A job-level `if:` without a gate:** every ruled-out PR waits forever on three contexts that never report.
- **Keeping per-shard required contexts beside the gate:** every change to the shard count would need a ruleset edit.
- **A gate that reads `skipped` as a pass by itself:** a failed classifier also leaves skipped shards. The gate has to tell the two apart, as `e2e-engine-gate` does.
